counter_examples.text: the DXY fell about 40% from its Feb-1985 peak (164.72) with no crisis for 32 months
the crash came with the dollar FALLING (Louvre dispute)
the peso crisis peaked with the DXY at a then-record low (80.05)
LTCM's acute phase saw the DXY fall 8.9% on the yen-carry unwind
the DXY hit its all-time low (70.70) on the Bear Stearns weekend, seven months into the subprime crisis; it rose only after Lehman
the euro-crisis peak came with the DXY at the bottom of the band
SVB (2023), the yen-carry unwind (Aug-2024) and the tariff shock (Apr-2025) all saw the dollar fall

honesty: Every historical number here is in-sample: the study examined all of 1971-2026 before the panel was built.
Crises cluster: 25 crises (A25), 16 onsets (C16), 5 dollar-funding squeezes (N5); counts are of months or episodes, not independent draws.
Reverse causality: the dollar rises because forced deleveraging buys dollars, so 'dollar up then crisis' and 'crisis then dollar up' look alike.
The deceleration rule's parameters were chosen on 2008, 2020 and 2022; its record on unseen 1973-2005 monthly data shows no edge.
The dollar-scramble markers (funding easing, gold's trough, the dollar's peak) date the end of the scramble, not the end of a crisis.
Johnson's claims are as relayed in the user's transcript; the Oct-2026 talk itself was not located.

momentum.caveat: in-sample on data the study had already examined; list-dependent; clusters, not independent draws; NOT validated
momentum.definition: 12-month change of the monthly-average DXY above +10%

momentum_ledger_basis: one row per momentum episode (first signal month after 12 quiet months); S&P and DXY as monthly averages, EM FX basket as-of the 28th, BAA minus GS10 monthly; reconstructed in-sample, not a forecast record

base_all_months.basis: every month 1971-2026 classified the same way: the unconditional share to compare the onset counts against

quadrant.definition: sign of the 3-month change of the monthly-average DXY and of the 10-year yield (GS10) into the onset month (finder C)

redollarisation.basis: log growth (100 x log-difference); BIS GLI Q.USD.3P.N.A.I.B.USD vs the Fed broad dollar, quarter-end; descriptive, not causal
redollarisation.corr_caveat: yoy changes overlap by three quarters, so the yoy correlations rest on roughly a quarter of the nominal sample; the non-overlapping qoq correlations are weaker (about -0.3)

scramble_rule.basis: outcomes on the rule's own index: dollar_further_rise_pct = broad dollar's max over the next 250 index days vs the firing day; spx_to_next_low_pct = S&P 500 from the firing close to its lowest close in the next 250 trading days; 3/6/12-month outcomes as-of calendar offsets

firings.reading: first wave of a two-wave scramble
re-arm firing (added after the 2008-09-22 miss); dollar scramble peaking, equity low still four months away
first wave of a policy grind (not a funding scramble)

monthly_null.window: 1973-2005 (monthly; unseen by the daily parameter choices)

params.index: Fed broad dollar DTWEXBGS, daily, on days with DTWEXBGS, DGS10 and VIXCLS all published (the frozen code/decel_realtime.py index)

scramble_rule.variant_live: re-arm (fires again inside the cooling window on a 1.5x bigger scramble; added after the 2008-09-22 miss)

vspike_timing.basis: 20-index-day change of the broad dollar on the rule's own index (days with DTWEXBGS, DGS10 and VIXCLS)
vspike_timing.note: on the full H.10 calendar the 2008 climb peak is 2008-10-24 (+12.3%, dollar +4.1% further)

vspike_timing.basis: 20-index-day change of the broad dollar on the rule's own index (days with DTWEXBGS, DGS10 and VIXCLS)

window_convention: an event at month m is followed by an onset if one falls in (m, m+H]; base rate = share of eligible months 1971-01..2026-10 minus H with an onset in (m, m+H]
